<description>
{
 "summary": "Validates the bantime parameter in the setban RPC to reject values that would cause an integer overflow when added to the current timestamp. If the sum of the relative duration and the current time exceeds the maximum 64-bit integer, the call now fails with an RPC_INVALID_PARAMETER error. A functional regression test is also added to rpc_setban.py.",
 "problem": "BanMan calculates the end of a ban as GetTime() plus the provided duration using signed 64-bit integers. Passing a relative bantime close to INT64_MAX causes a signed integer overflow (undefined behavior detected by UBSan); without sanitizers, the wrapped negative timestamp causes the ban to be treated as immediately expired and silently discarded despite the RPC reporting success.",
 "evidence": [
  "Author notes reproducible UBSan runtime error: 'src/banman.cpp:140:73: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 1790412558 + 9223372036854775807 cannot be represented in type int64_t' (description)",
  "Author confirms that on master, 'setban 1.2.3.5 add 9223372036854775807' returns success but listbanned remains empty because the ban is treated as expired (description)"
 ],

<category name="rpc" title="RPC / REST / ZMQ">
## Covers

The node's programmatic interfaces: JSON-RPC methods and their help and
argument handling, the HTTP server and authentication, `bitcoin-cli`,
the REST interface, and ZMQ notifications. Wallet RPCs are wallet first
and rpc second unless the change is to the RPC machinery itself. The
RPC/REST/ZMQ label is a strong prior.

Not rpc: the behavior an RPC merely exposes (that belongs to its area).

## What matters here

Compatibility first: changes that break or silently alter what existing
callers get back affect every application built on the node, so
correctness of returned data and the discipline around deprecations
matter most. Then security of the interface: authentication, exposure
of sensitive data, resource exhaustion through the HTTP server. Then
gaps that force applications into workarounds: missing fields or
methods that downstream software has asked for, with evidence they
asked. Then performance of hot methods that block explorers and
indexers call constantly. Then consistency and documentation of the
interface.

New methods without an external consumer asking rank low.
